result.summary: The image shows a typical urban residential and commercial street with sidewalks on both sides and parallel parking. While sidewalks are present, the environment lacks dedicated pedestrian crossing infrastructure or traffic calming measures in the visible mid-block section.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions
hazards.description: Continuous parallel parking on both sides of the street creates sightline obstructions between pedestrians and moving vehicles.

hazards.name: Lack of Crossing Infrastructure
hazards.description: No marked crossings or pedestrian warning signs are visible, which may lead to unsafe mid-block crossings, especially near the stopped school bus.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at intersections or potential crossing points to shorten crossing distance and improve visibility by 'daylighting' the corners.

interventions.title: Mid-block Crossing
interventions.description: If the distance between intersections is significant, a marked mid-block crossing with high-visibility markings and signage should be considered.

interventions.title: Speed Humps
interventions.description: Implement vertical speed control measures to reduce vehicle speeds in this mixed-use/residential context.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a two-lane roadway with a marked midblock crosswalk and on-street parallel parking. Safety is compromised by significant visual obstructions from a large school bus and parked vehicles, as well as a wide curb cut for an adjacent parking lot that creates additional conflict points.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: A large school bus and parked cars block sightlines between pedestrians at the crosswalk and oncoming drivers.

hazards.name: Unprotected Midblock Crossing
hazards.description: The marked crosswalk lacks any vertical signage or signals to alert drivers to the presence of pedestrians.

hazards.name: Wide Curb Cut
hazards.description: A wide entrance to an off-street parking lot creates a large conflict zone where vehicles cross the sidewalk.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at the crosswalk to reduce crossing distance and move pedestrians into the driver's line of sight beyond parked vehicles.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk Markings
interventions.description: Upgrade the existing parallel lines to a continental or ladder pattern to increase the conspicuity of the crossing.

interventions.title: Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons (RRFB)
interventions.description: Install pedestrian-activated flashing beacons to increase driver yield rates at this midblock crossing.

result.summary: The image shows a signalized urban intersection with marked zebra crosswalks and pedestrian signals. While basic infrastructure is present, the wide crossing distance and lack of physical traffic calming measures or refuge islands increase pedestrian exposure to vehicular traffic.

hazards.name: Long crossing distance
hazards.description: The width of the roadway requires pedestrians to be in the path of vehicles for an extended period without a refuge.

hazards.name: Sightline obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles near the intersection corners may block the view between drivers and pedestrians waiting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image, near the church

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions (bulb-outs) to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to ensure clear sightlines for all road users.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment consists of a continuous sidewalk along a mixed-use block, though the walkway is cluttered with obstructions and lacks a buffer from traffic. Parked vehicles significantly limit visibility between the sidewalk and the roadway, and there are no visible designated crossing points.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: Large parked vehicles in the foreground and along the curb obstruct the view of pedestrians for oncoming traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Left foreground and along the curb line.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: Fencing, bins, and vehicles parked in the frontage area restrict the clear walking width of the sidewalk.
hazards.location_in_image: Center-right in front of the restaurant.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at the nearest intersections to improve sightlines and reduce crossing distances.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Protection
interventions.description: Use bollards or planters to prevent vehicles from parking on or encroaching into the pedestrian clear zone.
